FIB_PLUS	<p>4a69_e21e</p> <h4>Three-Point Test Cross Problem</h4><p>A test cross is a way to explore the relationship between genes and their respective alleles. It is a useful tool for genetic mapping and deciphering the inheritance of traits. Specifically, a three-point test cross examines three (3) genes at the same time to learn about their assortment in gamete formation.</p><p>A standard three-point test cross involves crossing a heterozygous organism for all three genes with an organism that is homozygous recessive for all three genes</p> <p>For this problem, a test cross using a fruit fly (<i>Drosophila melanogaster</i>) heterozygous for three genes was conducted to understand their genetic interactions.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>nerdy</i></span>' phenotype. A fruit fly that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene N</span> has large, prominent eyes that stand out, much like thick-rimmed glasses.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A fruit fly that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene R</span> has a reddish-brown color, much like rusted iron metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743dad;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #743dad;"><i>xanthic</i></span>' phenotype. A fruit fly that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743dad;">Gene X</span> has a fluorescent bright yellow coloring.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 2px solid black;"><tr><th align="center" style="border: 1px solid black; Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes N and R is [NR] cM (NR)</li><li>The distance between genes N and X is [NX] cM (NX)</li><li>The distance between genes R and X is [RX] cM (RX)</li><li>From this the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Hints</h6><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. For example, if the gene order is B - A - C, simply write "bac" or "cab".</li></ul>	NR	6		NX	30		RX	33		geneorder	rnx	xnr
